subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Teotihuacan: City of the Gods
description: A micro-lesson that makes Teotihuacan: City of the Gods usable.

hook.text: The largest city in the ancient Americas had 100,000 residents. Nobody knows what its builders called themselves.

buildup.text: Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun is the third-largest pyramid on Earth, built around 100 CE near modern Mexico City.

discovery.text: The city was planned on a grid with a two-mile central avenue. It had apartment complexes and a sewer system.

twist.text: Around 550 CE, the city was deliberately burned from the inside. Evidence suggests an internal revolt, not invasion.

climax.text: A robot exploring a tunnel under the Pyramid found liquid mercury and thousands of golden orbs in 2014.

punchline.text: A nameless people built an empire and burned it down themselves.

quiz.question: What evidence suggests Teotihuacan was destroyed from within?
options: Foreign weapons were found in the ruins
The city was burned from the inside, pointing to an internal revolt
Written records describe a civil war between priests and warriors
